sources.title: Duden, Rechtschreibregeln: Namen, D146
sources.claimVerified: Duden D146 states that compounds with multiple or multi-part names use hyphens, and lists Rio-de-la-Plata-Bucht among examples. It appears in the geographic-names section; the broader official §50 rule below is the direct basis for applying the pattern to a proper product name plus ID.
sources.verification: Official Duden page opened; D146 section and example were present.

sources.title: Rat für deutsche Rechtschreibung, Amtliches Regelwerk 2024, §50
sources.claimVerified: §50 states that a hyphen is set between all components of multi-part compounds whose initial components are proper names. Examples include Albrecht-Dürer-Allee, Heinrich-Heine-Platz, and Elbe-Havel-Kanal. This more directly supports German Open-Library-ID as a compound built from the multi-part proper name Open Library plus ID.
sources.verification: Official PDF opened and §50 text/examples located.

sources.title: Open Library official home page
sources.claimVerified: The official site uses “Open Library” as its two-word name in the page heading and project description.
sources.verification: Official home page opened; exact spelling observed.

determination.reason: The source is the exact two-word product name followed by ID. Hyphenated compounding retains the proper name components; the checker’s exact-space substring rule does not account for German compounding. Duden D146 supports the hyphen pattern by example, while official §50 supplies the broader proper-name rule.
